title: CV32E40P ALU
description: The execution-stage ALU of the OpenHW Group's CV32E40P RISC-V core: the RV32IM operations plus the XPULP extensions (two 16-bit or four 8-bit SIMD lanes, bit manipulation and counting, shuffle and pack, clip) and a multi-cycle serial divider behind a ready handshake, 57 opcodes in all. The starting point is the upstream RTL flattened into one file, with no logic changes.
flow: Yosys synthesis and OpenROAD static timing analysis on ASAP7. Correctness: the gate-level netlist is re-simulated against the upstream ALU embedded in the testbench, which compares the ready handshake in every cycle and the results whenever upstream is ready, so the schedule stays cycle-identical to upstream; 20,000 recorded vectors, a divider sweep over every divisor and dividend bit length and 1,000,000 fixed-seed random operations; all checks must pass.

notes.glm-5.2: Default effort, pinned to Z.AI. Through OpenRouter a request without an effort setting behaves like thinking off: the default, high and off rows all produce 1k to 2k output tokens per step, and their results are within noise of each other. The high-effort runs are recorded but held back from the table.

footnotes: Rows labelled as measured before the current suite are earlier data (pre-v1 seed runs from July 2026 with an unpackaged rtlscout, or suite-v1 runs from October 2026 without the provider pin and completion cap). Each is replaced when reruns of that entry under the current suite are published.
All entries were called through OpenRouter without prompt caching, so every step pays for its full input.
